question.prompt: For any positive integer \(M,\) the notation \(M!\) denotes the product of the integers \(1\) through \(M.\) What is the largest integer \(n\) for which \(5^n\) is a factor of the sum: \[98!+99!+100!\]

solutions.explanation:
The three factorials share the factor \(98!\). Factoring it out turns the sum into a product whose factors of \(5\) we can count:
\[
\begin{aligned}
98!+99!+100!
&=98!\bigl(1+99+100\cdot99\bigr)\\
&=98!\cdot10000.
\end{aligned}
\]
In \(98!=1\cdot2\cdots98\), only multiples of \(5\) contribute factors of \(5\). There are \(19\) such multiples, namely \(5,10,\ldots,95\), contributing one factor each. The numbers \(25,50,75\) each contribute one additional factor because they are multiples of \(25=5^2\). No number in the product is a multiple of \(125=5^3\), so there are no further factors of \(5\).

Thus \(98!\) contains exactly \(19+3=22\) factors of \(5\). Also,
\[
10000=10^4=2^4\cdot5^4,
\]
so the other factor contributes four more. The sum therefore contains exactly \(22+4=26\) factors of \(5\). It is divisible by \(5^{26}\), and after removing those factors the remaining integer is not divisible by \(5\), so \(5^{27}\) cannot divide it.

The largest integer is \(n=26\), choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Factor the sum and count factors of five
